title: Improving scalable oversight with co-trained monitors
abstract: arXiv:2609.36049v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Worker-monitor setups are a promising approach to AI oversight, but training workers against fixed monitors can incentivize monitor evasion. We study whether this failure mode can be avoided by co-training the monitor alongside the worker, and explore both supervised and self-supervised approaches. In the supervised setting, we prove a characterization: monitoring is possible with vanishing error and query rates exactly when the class of possible monitor functions has finite Littlestone dimension. This connects worker monitoring with an established literature on adversarial online learning. For self-supervision, we propose a co-training procedure based on test-time distillation: the monitor uses additional test-time compute to generate training labels, then trains its standard-compute policy on those labels. For majority-vote labels, we give a finite-sample sharpening guarantee under adaptive worker distributions with action coverage,

translated_title: 通过协同训练的监督者改进可扩展监督
translated_abstract: 工作者-监督者架构是AI监督的一种有前景的方法，但针对固定监督者训练工作者可能会激励监督者规避行为。我们研究是否可以通过让监督者与工作者协同训练来避免这种失败模式，并探索了有监督和自监督两种方法。在有监督设置中，我们证明了一个刻画：当且仅当可能的监督者函数类具有有限Littlestone维数时，才能以消失的错误率和查询率实现有效监督。这将工作者监督与对抗性在线学习领域的成熟文献联系起来。对于自监督，我们提出了一种基于测试时蒸馏的协同训练程序：监督者使用额外的测试时计算来生成训练标签，然后在这些标签上训练其标准计算策略。对于多数投票标签，我们在具有动作覆盖的自适应工作者分布下给出了有限样本锐化保证。
tldr: 与工作者协同训练监督者可避免监督规避问题，其中有监督情形可用Littlestone维数刻画可监控性，自监督情形则提出基于测试时蒸馏的协同训练方法并获得有限样本保证。
en_tdlr: Co-training monitors alongside workers avoids monitor evasion; supervised monitoring is possible exactly when the monitor function class has finite Littlestone dimension, and a test-time distillation co-training procedure yields finite-sample sharpening guarantees.
